title: Managed Backup: outage credit entitlement
content:
For Managed Backup, the outage credit entitlement basis governs customer request registration, source review, credit posting.

## Policy clauses

For an outage service credit financial posting, an approved review has decision eligible and positive approved credit amount for the exact source charge; this gate does not constrain filing or reviewing the request.

For an outage service credit request being filed, the outage claim is filed no later than outage claim filing period after the official incident closes.

For a newly filed claim, fixed handling time is its notice filing time; the request is recorded immediately.

Later review and credit use that recorded notice filing time to evaluate the same boundary, so a timely request does not expire while awaiting review.

Add outage claim filing period UTC calendar dates to official incident closure time, preserving its time of day; calendar dates are counted without substituting business days or elapsed-hour periods.

Equality at the deadline qualifies; a later claim is rejected without a credit.

The provider incident must be completed, with cause outside excluded outage causes.

Availability at or above availability target percentage gives no credit.

Below the target choose the first descending availability credit bands entry whose minimum is no greater than the recorded availability percentage.

Multiply the original source charge pretax amount by that fraction; subtract the cumulative pretax service-credit amount component of prior credits for that exact source, and cap total service credits at cumulative outage credit cap fraction of that original net amount.

Floor the additional credit at zero and round with monetary decimal precision and rounding convention.

Apply the original tax component proportionately.

A review writes its nonnegative approved result; a financial credit writes the negative approved amount only after that approved review exists.

This service-credit branch applies only to source business subtype outage service credit; billing correction rules apply only to source business subtype correction.

Excluded incidents, ineligible reviews and zero remaining entitlement result in no financial write.

A request for consequential-loss compensation is not covered.

A service-credit financial posting requires an approved review with decision eligible and positive approved credit amount; the request and incident alone cannot authorize the financial posting.

## Authoritative evidence

Before customer request registration, system records must establish this condition for the proposed action: For an outage service credit request being filed, the outage claim is filed no later than outage claim filing period after the official incident closes.

The evidence identifies Event reference, Official incident closure time, Notice filing time. Match the action to that evidence by Event reference; these references identify the same proposed business objects.

Add outage claim filing period UTC calendar dates to official incident closure time, preserving its time of day; calendar dates are counted without substituting business days or elapsed-hour periods. The comparison uses the fixed handling clock and includes equality at the boundary.

Before credit posting, system records must establish this condition for the proposed action: For an outage service credit financial posting, an approved review has decision eligible and positive approved credit amount for the exact source charge; this gate does not constrain filing or reviewing the request.

The evidence identifies Event reference, Original source reference, Status, Decision, Approved credit amount. Match the action to that evidence by Original source reference; these references identify the same proposed business objects.

The cumulative pretax service-credit ceiling is the original source pretax amount multiplied by its applicable credit cap fraction.

## Basis Q&A

**What is the stated entry basis?** For an outage service credit financial posting, an approved review has decision eligible and positive approved credit amount for the exact source charge; this gate does not constrain filing or reviewing the request.

## Hypothetical case

In a hypothetical claim, filing exactly at the incident closure time advanced by the applicable number of UTC calendar dates meets the deadline. Filing at a later instant fails it. A timely filing remains timely when the review occurs after that deadline, because review uses the recorded filing time. These timing results alone do not authorize a financial credit.
